## Identity
Extensive personal YouTube activity log spanning nearly two decades. Primary media consumption channel for news, politics, comedy, and cultural commentary. Data from two Google Takeout HTML exports: the original 2007–2025 pull (below, unchanged) and a fresh export the operator located in Drive and supplied directly on 2026-07-20, extending coverage to July 20, 2026 and adding a genuinely new finding — see "Extended coverage" below, which should be read before trusting any of the older per-year tables at face value.

> **REVISED [2026-07-20]:** the older export's own "Watched" counts (this page's 17,302, and the 17,426 total-events figure cited on [[wiki/mind/synthesis/intake-constancy]] and [[wiki/mind/synthesis/totality-themes]]) were never broken out by whether the "watch" was a real video or a served ad impression. A verified re-parse this session found **14.1% of the old export's 15,149 "Watched" entries are Google Ads** ("From Google Ads" tagged, no real engagement implied) — meaning the true count of videos genuinely watched is closer to 13,011, and every per-year/per-channel table below is Watched-block counts, not ad-filtered counts. This doesn't overturn the page's interpretive content (the channel/category analysis was necessarily done on real, titled, non-ad content, since ads rarely carry recognizable channel names), but the raw volume figures should be read as an upper bound on real engagement, not the engagement itself. This matters far more in the newly-covered period — see below.

## Extended coverage: August 2025 – July 2026 (new, 2026-07-20)

The operator spotted a fresh Google Takeout export in Drive (created 2026-07-20, split across two zip parts, the larger exceeding this session's download tooling and requiring a manual re-upload of just the `watch-history.html` file) and asked for a comparison against the export below. The new file runs 2007 through **July 20, 2026** — extending real coverage by nearly a full year past the old export's last entry (July 25, 2025) — and, cross-checked entry-by-entry against the old file, surfaces a genuine finding rather than just more of the same data:

**A ~100-day near-total gap in this account's real watches, Nov 8 2025 – Feb 15 2026.** Splitting every "Watched" block into real content versus Google Ads impressions (a distinction the old export's published counts never made — see the REVISED note above) shows exactly **one** real video watched between November 8, 2025 and February 15, 2026: "Man in Cave (Reupload)," on Nov 8 itself. Every other logged event in that ~100-day window — 78 of them — is an ad impression, frequently in dense back-to-back clusters with zero real videos between them (e.g. ~40 consecutive ads on Jan 4, 2026 across 3.5 hours; another ~15-ad cluster on Dec 26, 2025).

> **Operator correction (2026-07-20):** this Google account has multiple YouTube accounts tied to it, and the operator confirms he was almost certainly watching on a different one of those accounts during this window — this specific export just doesn't cover it. Not a real behavioral gap; a single-account coverage limitation. The dense ad-only clusters (a device apparently still logged in and passively serving ads while the real viewing happened elsewhere) are exactly consistent with that explanation. **This caveat applies more broadly than just this one window** — every count on this page, old and new export alike, is single-account data; total real watching across all the operator's YouTube accounts combined is confirmed higher than any figure below. Treat every number on this page as a lower bound on true activity, not a census, until a consolidated multi-account export exists.

This window sits directly inside the corpus's own highest-intensity Annie-relationship crisis stretch: the December 2025 message-volume peak ([[wiki/timeline/periods/dec-2025-spike]], 4,657 messages, near-parity reconciliation attempt), the sharp January–February 2026 engagement asymmetry that followed it, and the run-up to [[wiki/timeline/events/march-2026-terminal-phase|March 2026's "most concentrated gaslighting" fortnight]]. Real watching resumes gradually after: 9 videos in March 2026, then a clear rebound — 243 in April, 136 in May.

**A second, related finding: the June–July 2026 numbers look like a huge activity spike but mostly aren't.** Raw block counts alone would suggest a massive surge (1,036 events in June, 1,616 in the first 20 days of July) — but 80.3% of June's entries and 96.4% of July's are ads, not real watches. Real content watched: 204 in June, only 58 in the first 20 days of July. The apparent "explosion" is overwhelmingly ad-volume noise. Whether that leaves July 2026 above or below true (multi-account) baseline consumption is now an open question rather than a settled comparison — see the multi-account caveat above, which applies to the historical ~11.58/day figure just as much as to this window.

| Month | Real watches | Ad impressions | Ad % |
|-------|-------------:|----------------:|-----:|
| 2025-09 | 191 | 12 | 5.9% |
| 2025-10 | 112 | 6 | 5.1% |
| 2025-11 | 1 | 13 | 92.9% |

| 2026-06 | 204 | 832 | 80.3% |
| 2026-07 (through 20th) | 58 | 1,558 | 96.4% |

**Top channels, real watches only, Aug 2025 – Jul 2026:** Breaking Points (112), LastWeekTonight (95), The Majority Report w/ Sam Seder (93), Tor's Cabinet of Curiosities (91), We're In Hell (42), JREG (23), Tucker Carlson (22), STRANGE ÆONS (22), exurb1a (19), DJ Peach Cobbler (17), HasanAbi (16), Chapo Trap House (13). The political-commentary spine (Breaking Points, LastWeekTonight, Majority Report, HasanAbi) is continuous with the 2022+ diet already documented below; Tor's Cabinet of Curiosities, We're In Hell, JREG, STRANGE ÆONS, exurb1a, and DJ Peach Cobbler are new-to-the-corpus names not previously catalogued in this page's channel tables, plus a late-June 2026 late-night cluster of 2000s pop-punk nostalgia (Green Day and Fall Out Boy "AOL Sessions" live videos, June 30).

**Minor discrepancy, not a data-integrity concern:** 240 URLs present in the old export near its July 2025 cutoff don't appear in the new one — spot-checked, every sampled example is an ad impression from the same July 23–25, 2025 boundary window (KAYAK, Arby's, Harbor Freight, insurance/pharma spots). Google's ad-activity logging is evidently not perfectly deterministic run-to-run at export boundaries; this affects only a handful of ad rows, not real watch data.

## Content Patterns

- **Political / News Heavy**: Dominant categories include progressive/left media critique, current events analysis, institutional skepticism, and election/Trump-era coverage (301 Trump title hits). Ties directly to self-corpus political identity as "insufferable politics sicko".
- **Comedy & Satire**: Significant LastWeekTonight / John Oliver style, Vaush commentary, and internet humor; early shock radio (O&A).
- **Radio/Podcast Archives**: Largest early volume — Opie & Anthony / TESD / Bennington universe archives. Preference for long-form conversational/deep-dive.
- **Music / Entertainment**: YT Music section ~2,370 watches (2022-2025 heavy); scattered videos and live. Aligns with [[wiki/interests/favorites/music]] electronic/bass cluster.
- **Historical / Educational**: Mr. Beat (civics, history) 111 watches (98 in 2023); INTO THE FRAY early (101).
- **YT Music vs Main**: Recent shift includes dedicated music platform use alongside commentary.

The media diet reflects sustained interest in power structures, media literacy, and cultural commentary — core to the "politics sicko" persona documented in [[wiki/self/twitter]] and [[wiki/mind/synthesis/political-psyops]].

## Consumption Patterns and Date Clusters

**Era 1: 2011–2013 Radio + Exploratory (peak volume 2012 3.5k)**  
O&A / Opie Radio + O&A archives (hundreds), INTO THE FRAY (71 in 2012). Shock radio nostalgia + early online video. Coincides with FB likes for ODESZA (Oct 2014 close), electronic music pages (JAUZ, Borgore, Spinnin' Records, Flying Lotus), comedy clubs (Gotham, Comedy Cellar, The Stand).

**Era 2: 2014–2021 Lull + Spikes**  
Low baseline (100s/yr); LastWeekTonight entry (2017/2020), small 2020 election bump. Music consumption via main YT + FB likes for comedy (Comedy Bang Bang, Nathan For You) and some politics (AOC, Chris Cuomo, VICE TV).

**Era 3: 2022–2025 Resurgence + Focused Diet (2k+/yr + YT Music)**  
Modern left tube dominant: Vaush (177 in 2023), Majority Report (Sam Seder), David Pakman, Breaking Points (38 in 2025), HasanAbi, Some More News. History ed: Mr. Beat 98 in 2023. Satire sustained. YT Music 691 (2022) + 987 (2025). 2023 May peak month 396. Ties to post-employment block processing, skepticism themes.

**Patterns observed**:
- Archive binge (O&A long sessions) vs. short-form modern commentary.
- Shift from broad exploratory (radio + into the fray) to targeted political + educational.
- Persistent "sicko" engagement with power/media critique across eras.
- Music/electronic interest evidenced indirectly via FB likes 2012-14 + YT Music volume recent; no direct ODESZA in YT titles but temporal alignment.
- Self channel watches (Dan Frank 22) + production adjacent.

## Relation to Existing Self Data

- **High volume periods (2012–2013, 2022–2023, 2025)** align with or contrast existing self periods.
  - Early 2010s peak coincides with pre-employment stability and high digital engagement.
  - 2021 low activity during [[wiki/timeline/periods/2021-2023-employment-block]].
  - 2022–2023 resurgence during later employment block.
  - 2025 activity (1,871 through July) is substantial and may relate to post-closure processing.
- Complements [[wiki/self/twitter]] (public political expression mirroring "sicko" diet) and [[wiki/self/favorites]] / [[wiki/interests/favorites/music]] (music consumption overlap; electronic/bass via 2014 likes + YT Music).
- Reinforces [[wiki/mind/concepts/conflict-architecture]]: repeated engagement with content that litigates institutions, power, and narrative.
- Ties to [[wiki/self/facebook]]: FB pages_you_ve_liked (196 total) includes ODESZA (2014-10-17), comedy clubs, AOC, Chris Cuomo, VICE TV, Trump White House archive, electronic labels (DIM MAK, Buygore). 2012-2014 likes align exactly with Era 1 radio + music window. See [[wiki/self/facebook]] and subpages.
- Attention patterns: Long sessions with archive channels (O&A, radio) suggest comfort with extended conversational/deep-dive formats. Cross [[wiki/mind/synthesis/vertical-authority-skepticism]] and [[wiki/mind/synthesis/political-psyops]].
- Location cross: Media consumption portable across PA roots / NYC chapter (high loc visits 2017-19, 2022-23 align YT spikes).
- Ancestry roots: PA/Fayette cluster provides stable "home base" for early digital (YT) + loc data.

## Media as Longitudinal Witness
YT history functions as objective "millennial digital witness" channel (see [[wiki/mind/synthesis/millennial-digital-witness]]): records shift in information diet from pre-social shock radio archives (O&A 2011-14) through 2020s online left video essay / commentary explosion. Parallels FB likes (2014 ODESZA/electronic), Twitter political output, and context-core periods. Provides measurable evidence of sustained skepticism, media literacy, and cultural bridge position without relying on self-report. Complements totality-themes corpus (sources include this YT + loc + FB + twitter). No contradictions with core political identity.

## Timeline Highlights

| Period | Observation |
|--------|-------------|
| 2007–2010 | Earliest likes/dislikes (sparse). Includes music and early internet content. FB account 2007. |
| 2011–2013 | Highest sustained volume (peak 2012). Heavy O&A radio archives + INTO THE FRAY. Early politics signals. |
| 2014–2021 | Lower baseline with small spikes (2020 election). LastWeekTonight entry. FB ODESZA + electronic/comedy likes (2012-14 window). 2019-21 NYC loc high but YT low. |
| 2022–2023 | Major resurgence (2k+ each year). Vaush/Majority Report/Pakman dominant + Mr. Beat history. YT Music ramp. Aligns employment block later phase + loc resurgence. |
| 2024–2025 | Continued high engagement (2025 1.8k to July). Breaking Points, sustained politics/satire + YT Music peak (987). Post-closure + PA return. |

## Notes

This is one of the richest longitudinal behavioral datasets available. It provides objective measurement of media diet over 15+ years. 17k+ watched events + channel metadata + date clusters enable precise cross-corpus mapping (FB likes 2014 ODESZA alignment, loc mobility peaks, Twitter "sicko" output, periods).

**New connections summarized (media as witness channel):** YT serves as primary longitudinal witness to evolution of political skepticism and digital media consumption, bridging pre-smartphone radio nostalgia to LLM-era commentary consumption. Direct temporal overlap with FB 2012-2014 likes (electronic music ODESZA etc, comedy clubs) during Era 1; resurgence mirrors context-core life events and loc home-base returns. Feeds [[wiki/mind/synthesis/millennial-digital-witness]], [[wiki/mind/synthesis/totality-themes]], [[wiki/mind/synthesis/vertical-authority-skepticism]]. Cross to [[wiki/self/location-history]] (portable consumption across PA/NYC), [[wiki/self/facebook]] (likes + profile politics/education), [[wiki/interests/favorites/music]] (eclecticism validation).

plain.title: YouTube Watch History (2007–2026)
plain.body:
**The short version.** Dan's YouTube history goes back nearly twenty years and
is one of the most detailed records of his attention that exists. It shows a
loud early stretch built almost entirely around archived shock-radio shows, a
long quiet middle, and a big return in 2022 built around left-wing political
commentary. But the headline numbers are not what they look like. A large share
of the logged "watches" are advertisements, not videos he chose. And the whole
export only covers one of his several YouTube accounts. **Every count here is a
floor, not a total.**

## Two things that break the raw numbers

Anyone reading this record should know these before reading any figure in it.

**First: a lot of the "watches" are ads.** The original export logged 17,302
"Watched" events. When someone actually checked which of those were real videos
and which were served advertisements, **14.1% of the 15,149 entries turned out
to be Google Ads.** That puts the real count of videos he chose to watch closer
to **13,011**. None of the per-year tables in the full entry were ever filtered
this way, so they are an upper bound on real engagement, not the engagement
itself.

**Second, and larger: this is one account out of several.** The Google login has
multiple YouTube accounts attached. That means every number in this record —
old export and new — describes only what happened on this one account. Dan has
confirmed that his real total viewing across all of them is higher than any
figure here. Until somebody produces a combined export covering all the
accounts, the honest reading is that **these are lower bounds, not a census.**

That second point is not a footnote. It arrived as a correction to a finding
this record had already drawn, and it changed what the finding meant.

## The gap that looked like a collapse and wasn't

Splitting real videos from ad impressions turned up something dramatic: between
**November 8, 2025 and February 15, 2026** — about 100 days — this account
records exactly **one** real video watched. That was "Man in Cave (Reupload)",
on November 8 itself.

Everything else logged in that window was an advertisement. **78 of them**,
often in dense back-to-back runs with no real videos in between — roughly 40
consecutive ads on January 4, 2026 across three and a half hours, another
cluster of about 15 on December 26, 2025.

That looked like a person who had stopped watching anything. And it sat exactly
on top of one of the most intense documented stretches in his personal life,
which made it read like evidence of a shutdown.

**It wasn't.** Dan confirmed he was almost certainly watching on a different one
of his YouTube accounts during that window; this export simply does not cover
it. The dense ad-only clusters fit that perfectly — a device still logged in,
passively being served ads, while the real watching happened somewhere the
export cannot see.

This is worth sitting with, because it is the clearest example of how the whole
record can mislead. A hundred days of near-silence in a behavioural log is a
striking finding. It was an artifact of which account got exported.

## The other thing that looks like a spike and isn't

The most recent months appear to show an enormous surge in activity — 1,036
logged events in June 2026, and 1,616 in just the first twenty days of July.

Filter the ads out and it mostly disappears. **80.3%** of June's entries and
**96.4%** of July's are advertisements. Real videos watched: **204** in June and
only **58** in the first twenty days of July.

Here is the monthly picture once the two are separated:

| Month | Real watches | Ads | Ads as share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2025-09 | 191 | 12 | 5.9% |
| 2025-10 | 112 | 6 | 5.1% |
| 2025-11 | 1 | 13 | 92.9% |
| 2025-12 | 0 | 18 | 100.0% |
| 2026-01 | 0 | 43 | 100.0% |

Whether the recent months are actually above or below his normal viewing is now
an open question rather than a settled one, because of the multi-account

## What he actually watched, in three eras

**2011–2013: the radio archive years.** These are the two loudest years in the
entire log — 3,538 logged events in 2012, 2,742 in 2013 — and they are not
scattered browsing. They are substantially one subject: fan-uploaded archives of
the Opie & Anthony shock-radio universe. Three separate fan-archive channels sit
near the top of the all-time list. That is the signature of somebody working
through a back catalogue until it runs out, not returning to a favourite.

**2014–2021: the long quiet.** Volume drops hard and stays down — 708 in 2014,
353 in 2015, 122 in 2016, and a low of **78 in 2019**. There is a small bump in
2020 around the election (295), and Last Week Tonight enters the picture. 2021,
during a difficult employment stretch, sits at 158.

**2022–present: politics.** The return is sharp and it has a clear shape:
**2,256** logged events in 2022 and **2,622** in 2023. The channels are left
political commentary — Vaush (177 watches in 2023 alone), The Majority Report,
David Pakman, Breaking Points, HasanAbi, Some More News — alongside civics and
history from Mr. Beat (98 in 2023). Trump appears in **301** video titles;
"election" in 61. Music also moves onto YouTube's dedicated music service in
this period, around 2,370 watches, peaking at 987 in 2025.

The most recent year, counting real watches only, keeps that spine: Breaking
Points 112, Last Week Tonight 95, The Majority Report 93, plus names new to this
record — Tor's Cabinet of Curiosities (91), We're In Hell (42), JREG (23),
STRANGE ÆONS (22), exurb1a (19). There is also a late-night cluster of 2000s
pop-punk nostalgia on June 30, 2026: Green Day and Fall Out Boy live sessions.

Across the whole log there are **4,146** unique channels — wide breadth
alongside a handful of very deep niches.

## What this record is good for

Used carefully, it is an unusually honest witness, because he was not writing it
down — it accumulated whether or not he was paying attention to it. It tracks
the shift in where his information came from, from pre-social-media radio
archives through the 2020s explosion of online political video. It lines up with
other records of the same years: his Facebook likes from 2012 to 2014 match the
radio-and-electronic-music era exactly.

One thing it can date but not explain: the 2022-onward political viewing is the
downstream trace of a political shift the message record dates precisely to
August 2020. The watch history shows that the turn **stuck**. It does not show
where it came from.

## What we still don't know

- **The big one: there is no combined export.** Every count here covers a single
  account. Until all of the accounts are exported together, no figure on this
  record can be treated as a total — including the daily averages other entries
  have quoted from it.

- **The old per-year tables were never ad-filtered.** Every year-by-year number
  from the original export mixes real videos with ad impressions. Only the most
  recent stretch has been properly separated.

- **240 entries near the old export's cutoff vanished from the new one.** Every
  sampled example was an ad impression from the same three-day boundary window,
  so this looks like Google's ad logging simply not being identical run to run.
  It affects a handful of ad rows, not real viewing data.
